title: Marc Lou's tech stack: pick one boring stack, never change it, ship faster
summary: Marc breaks down the simple, cheap stack behind his 21 products (Next.js, Tailwind, daisyUI, MongoDB, Stripe, Vercel). His core argument is that the choice barely matters: sticking with one stack makes you comfortable and fast. He also shows how little he spends on infrastructure and monitoring.

principles.text: Tech stack doesn't matter. Pick one and stick to it to get comfortable and ship faster.
principles.quote: **Tech stack doesn’t matter.** Pick one and stick to it. You’ll get comfortable and ship much faster.

principles.text: Don't chase design trends; a component library with a few themes is enough for a solopreneur.
principles.quote: Design trends give birth to new UI components every day. It’s a distraction for solopreneurs. daisyUI has 20+ themes and all the components, that’s enough.

principles.text: Choose infrastructure with no maintenance so a new project is a clone away.
principles.quote: I don’t have to install packages or maintain an OS. I clone a NextJS project and I have a scalable API for my micro SaaS in seconds.

principles.text: Keep monitoring minimal: simple traffic analytics, deploy logs, and occasional DB queries for the rest.
principles.quote: I query the database using relevant filters for advanced monitoring, like split testing. But I rarely do that.

principles.text: Never change your stack; consistency is how one person runs 21 products.
principles.quote: I never change my tech stack.
